features.source_feature: Table 108 distinguishes Type 1, MMType1, Type3 and TrueType simple font routes by Subtype; it is a dictionary classification map, not a demand to reject unsupported programs.
features.implementation: crates/pdf-font/src/loading/opening.rs simple-font dispatch; crates/pdf-font/src/type1.rs; crates/pdf-font/src/truetype.rs; Type 3 is separately loaded.
assertions: crates/pdf-font tests in type1.rs/truetype.rs for their respective parser paths
features.assertion_assessment: The sampled routes exercise actual parser/font consumers. Table 108 is an index of supported font types and carries no independent literal rendering oracle beyond the route-specific suites.
features.verdict: No separate Table 108 behavior defect identified in this bounded pass.
features.residuals: Not a full route or malformed-subtype audit; producer classification constraints alone do not establish reader rejection behavior.

features.source_feature: Table 109 lists Type/Subtype, BaseFont, FirstChar, LastChar, Widths, FontDescriptor, Encoding, ToUnicode. Widths correspond to the declared character-code interval, are in thousandths of text-space units, and the text says they shall be consistent with program widths. FirstChar/LastChar/Widths and FontDescriptor are required with the Standard-14 PDF 1.0-1.7 exception stated in the cells. EC3 #106 removes the FontDescriptor indirect-reference restriction. The surrounding compatibility paragraph for missing glyph-width definitions was replaced/demoted by #47/#48; do not treat that historical prose as an active override of the table.
features.ledger: doc/conformance/ledger.toml §9.6.2.1 plus simple-font metric and descriptor rows
features.implementation: crates/pdf-font/src/loading/opening.rs::load_simple; crates/pdf-font/src/metrics.rs; direct FontDescriptor is obtained through document.get_key(...).as_dict().
assertions: crates/pdf-font/src/metrics.rs tests for stated/default MissingWidth and width selection
features.assertion_assessment: The exact-xref simple_metrics test explicitly crosses direct and indirect FontDescriptor forms and indirect Widths/MissingWidth references, then checks A/B/C/D against literal widths. This is direct evidence for #106's dictionary directness on a simple TrueType consumer. Separate embedded-font tests compare actual program advances to PDF widths. These do not demand rejection for producer-inconsistent metrics.
features.verdict: No directness gap or runtime defect found. Effective Table 109 requirements are implemented in sampled width consumption; historical compatibility text is not used to enlarge the current reader mandate.
features.residuals: The consistency requirement is producer-facing; tests verify the stated/program relationship for sampled valid programs, not reader rejection of inconsistent input. This pass does not enumerate every optional descriptor metric. Table109 Name is a version-dependent deprecated entry on328; no new consumer assertion for that identity cell is claimed.

features.source_feature: Table 112 allows an Encoding name or dictionary. For dictionary form, BaseEncoding and Differences have their specified optionality; named bases are constrained to MacRomanEncoding, MacExpertEncoding, WinAnsiEncoding. §9.6.5.1 defines the default-base route based on embedded/built-in encoding and Symbolic/Nonsymbolic descriptor state; Differences overlays code names from each integer start.
features.assertion_assessment: The named CFF tests assert discriminating glyph/code routes; separate embedded TrueType/public tests exercise Differences and cmap routing. Current audit evidence in simple_font_encoding_residual_current records a missing final StandardEncoding fill on a MacExpert-base TrueType dictionary with a positive Differences control, so this feature is not certified as uniformly passing. That is a pre-existing sibling finding and is intentionally not duplicated here.
features.verdict: Encoding dictionary routes are exercised, with the MacExpert-base residual tracked by the sibling shard; this cell review adds no new behavior finding.
features.residuals: This review does not re-audit the failing MacExpert-base case, Standard fill, byte-to-cmap language, or glyph-name resolution in general. Source SHOULD producer forms are not turned into reader rejection conditions.

features.source_feature: Table 113 at physical p342/printed p327 lists 16 code/name rows that distinguish Mac OS Roman from PDF MacRomanEncoding: notequal@173, infinity@176, lessequal@178, greaterequal@179, partialdiff@182, summation@183, product@184, pi@185, integral@186, Omega@189, radical@195, approxequal@197, Delta@198, lozenge@215, Euro@219, apple@240. The accompanying text says 15 additions plus the replacement of currency at 219.
features.ledger: doc/conformance/ledger.toml §9.6.5.4 / Mac OS Roman cmap mapping row
features.assertion_assessment: Current unit assertions establish cardinality, the single replacement at 219, and representative notequal/Euro mappings; they do not check every Table 113 row against its literal code. Implementation is a 16-item table copied from the standard. This is an assertion-completeness opportunity, not a detected mapping error.
features.verdict: No wrong mapping observed in source-to-code comparison. A compact literal all-16 mapping assertion is drafted to make the transcription independently checkable in CI.
features.residuals: No public rendering defect is claimed; the proposed unit test checks the encoding lookup table only, and does not certify all TrueType cmap behavior.
